history.dynasty: Tradition credits sage Vishwamitra (foundation), Adi Shankaracharya (8th c. renovation), and Maharaja Jawat Raj of Ratlam (medieval repairs - verify)
history.period: Legend claims 2000+ years; present marble structure 14th century with later partial rebuilding (verify)
history.summary: One of the very few temples in the world dedicated to Lord Brahma, and the most prominent of them. Per the Padma Purana legend, Brahma killed the demon Vajranabha with a lotus; three petals fell at Pushkar forming the three Pushkar lakes (Jyeshta, Madhya, Kanishtha - 'pushpa' flower + 'kar' hand). Brahma performed a yajna here, but his consort Savitri arrived late, so he married Gayatri to complete the ritual; an enraged Savitri cursed Brahma that he would never be worshipped except at Pushkar. The temple is governed by the Sanyasi (ascetic) sect priesthood; devotees bathe in Pushkar Lake before darshan. Many of Pushkar's old temples were destroyed under Aurangzeb (1658-1707) and rebuilt; the Brahma temple's current medieval fabric is attributed to Maharaja Jawat Raj of Ratlam (verify). name: Brahma Temple
town_description: Pushkar is an ancient pilgrimage town in Ajmer district on the edge of the Thar Desert, built around sacred Pushkar Lake, about 10 km from Ajmer city and 150 km from Jaipur. With 500+ temples and 52 ghats, it is one of the five sacred pilgrimage sites for Hindus and hosts the famous annual Pushkar Camel Fair on Kartik Poornima.

travel.road: About 10 km northwest of Ajmer on the Ajmer-Pushkar road; well connected by taxi and bus (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Kartik Poornima (October/November) for the Brahma festival and Pushkar Camel Fair - the peak pilgrimage season.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Winter 6:30 am-8:30 pm; summer 6:00 am-9:00 pm; closed 1:30-3:00 pm (verify).
